new_statements.quote: Nous essayerons de résumer ci-dessous les principales caractéristiques phonologiques et morphonologiques du bété. a) Sur le plan du système prosodique, notons les traits suivants: - la présence de quatre registres tonals distinctifs; - la stabilité du système tonal; - l'absence de tons modulés. b) Sur le plan de la structure syllabique, nous avons dégagé [...] les faits suivants: - l'existence de syllabes d'un centre à deux mores: CVV et ClV, la liquide étant syllabique dans cette structure et portant un ton distinctif; [...] c) Sur le plan de la structure lexicale, signalons: - le mono- ou dissyllabisme des lexèmes; - l'absence de lexèmes simples (non redoublés) trisyllabiques
new_statements.translation: We shall try to summarise below the main phonological and morphonological characteristics of Bété. a) As regards the prosodic system, we note the following features: the presence of four distinctive tonal registers; the stability of the tonal system; the absence of contour tones. b) As regards syllable structure, we have established [...] the existence of syllables with a two-mora centre, CVV and ClV, the liquid being syllabic in this structure and bearing a distinctive tone; [...] c) As regards lexical structure: lexemes are mono- or disyllabic; there are no simple (non-reduplicated) trisyllabic lexemes.

Items b)-f) (pp.191-193) cover syllable structure (CVV/ClV two-mora centres, syllab…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The authors' own summary of the prosodic system of Guibéroua (dakuya/Kosséoa) Bété is exclusively tonal: four level tones, no contour tones, tone-bearing morae including syllabic liquids; no word stress or accent is mentioned anywhere in the accessible pages, and the table of contents has no accent section. No rule for stress placement is stated.
new_statements.domain_note: CAUTION: only Rosetta-Project excerpts of the 215-page book were readable (pp. 5-7, 82, 85, 150-153, 191-215). The body sections that could carry an explicit remark on accent -- §1.1 'Segments et tons' pp. 10-13, §1.1.3 'Réalisation des tonèmes' p. 13, §1.2.5 'Note sur le mot phonologique' pp. 41-42 -- were NOT seen. The quoted passage is first-hand and characterises the language as a 4-register tone language, but 'no stress statement' is established only for the excerpt, not for the whole description.
new_statements.identity_note: Werle & Gbalehi 1976 describe the dakʷïe/dakuya dialect, parler de Kosséoa, 'groupe A' (Soubré-Guibéroua axis) = Glottolog guib1246 Guiberoua Béte / Ethnologue Central Bété [bet]. Gnizako's ɟībūō (jibuo) is the Soubré variety, also under [bet]/guib1246. Not to be confused with Daloa Bété [bev] dalo1238 (Zogbo's works; WALS wrongly maps its 'Bété' record, sourced from Werle & Gbalehi, to dalo1238) or Gagnoa Bété [btg] gagn1235 (Gbadi: Charette, Koopman, Zogbo 2005 dictionary; Kpɔkolo: Goprou; Guébie: Sande).

sources.note: Nothing in the accessible pages. Conclusions p.191 summarise the 'système prosodique' purely tonally: four distinctive tone registers, stable tonal system, no contour tones; CVV/ClV syllables with two morae, syllabic liquid bearing tone; lexemes mono- or disyllabic. TOC shows §1.1 'Segments et tons' (pp.10-13) and §1.2.5 'Note sur le mot phonologique' (p.41) but no section titled accent; those pages are not in the excerpt.
